phase-plan.purpose: Stop recursive workspace installs during docs-site lifecycle scripts so Vercel and other CI builds complete in normal time while still generating the KAPLAY iframe assets for build and local dev.
phase-plan.scope: In scope: docs-site install/build hook changes, KAPLAY asset bootstrap behavior, and verification with the Vercel-parity build path. Out of scope: broader dependency pruning, Payload MCP warnings, or unrelated phase 52 delivery API work.

file.description: Owns KAPLAY asset bootstrap logic and currently shells into a nested workspace install.
Defines lifecycle hooks that determine whether KAPLAY generation runs during install or only during build/dev.
Tracks task 52-05 ownership and execution state.

task.description: Trace the install loop to the nested workspace install inside ensure-kaplay-game.
Patch docs-site lifecycle hooks so install no longer re-enters workspace install while build/dev still generate KAPLAY assets.
Run Vercel-parity verification and capture the outcome in a summary doc.

questions.question: Should KAPLAY asset generation happen during install? No. It belongs in build/dev paths because install-time recursion is the failure source and the asset is not required merely to finish dependency installation.

decision.summary: docs-site lifecycle scripts must not invoke nested package-manager installs for other workspace packages.
decision.impact: Prevents recursive install/postinstall loops on Vercel and keeps CI timing predictable while preserving KAPLAY asset generation in prebuild/dev flows.

suggestion.gap: Phase 52 requirements do not explicitly state that CI/build hooks must avoid recursive workspace installs or install-time asset generation that is not required for dependency resolution.
suggestion.proposal: Add a delivery-pipeline requirement that docs-site deploy scripts remain non-recursive and separate dependency installation from optional asset generation.
